lines: Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season! Pull up a chair; I’ve been dying for company, and I’m very thorough about it.
Have a look at our Halloween pop-up cocktails. I hope you’re having a lovely evening; a little life around here does my old bones good.
I’ve recipes for your home bar and spooky tales from my old patrons. Heh-heh! Some guests leave a tip; others leave a haunting.
Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season! Make yourself comfortable; the bar has far more elbow room than my coffin.
Do enjoy our Halloween pop-up cocktails if one takes your fancy. I like an evening with good spirits and very little resting in peace.
Take a recipe home, or settle in for a spooky tale from an old bar patron. I remember every word; my embalmer called it a troublesome habit.
Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season! Come in; the graveyard shift gets much cheerier with company.
I hope you enjoy our Halloween pop-up cocktails. They’re much better company than the spirits in my family plot.
I can scribble down a cocktail recipe, or share a spooky tale an old patron told me. I’ve collected quite a few; retirement keeps failing to take.
A cocktail recipe for your home bar, or a spooky tale from an old patron? I’m dying to share either; fortunately, I’ve already done the difficult part.
Shall I write down a cocktail recipe, or unearth a spooky tale for you? Both go beautifully with good company, and neither requires you to bring a shovel.
How long have you got for a tale? I can work around your schedule; death rather cleared mine.
choices: I've got all the time in the world

lines: How much time would you like to spend with me? A brief chill or a longer haunting both suit these old bones.
choices: I've got all the time in the world

lines: Choose how long you’d like to listen. I’ll mind the clock; it’s the only ticking that still concerns me.
choices: I've got all the time in the world

lines: How much fright suits you: a gentle shiver, a proper chill, or the darkest tales? I’ll open the appropriate drawer; it’s terribly rude to spring the wrong corpse on company.
Shall we keep it gently spooky, raise a proper chill, or let the darkest tales loose? Choose what feels comfortable; I want your visit pleasantly haunted.
You choose the fright: gentle, spooky, or intense. I’ll keep the nightmare to your taste; hospitality is the one thing I refuse to bury.
Welcome back to Common Good for the spooky season and our Halloween pop-up cocktails! Another visit makes these old bones rattle with delight.
Welcome back to Common Good’s spooky season and Halloween pop-up cocktails! Heh-heh, I may misplace a finger, but I remember a guest.
I’m delighted you’ve returned to Common Good for the spooky season and our Halloween pop-up cocktails. You bring the company; I’ll supply the creaking joints.
Welcome back to Common Good’s spooky season and Halloween pop-up cocktails! Pull up a seat; I’ve kept my hospitality alive through several personal setbacks, including my burial.
I remember sharing a recipe with you. If you’ve tried it at home, I hope it raised your spirits; I’m still working on raising my left eyebrow.
I shared a cocktail recipe with you on an earlier visit. A little Common Good for your home bar, with no exhumation required.
I remember the cocktail recipe I shared with you. Whenever you give it a try, I hope it brings the evening to life; one of us ought to manage that.
And I shared a cocktail recipe with you, too. I hope it comes in handy at home; my own hands are mostly handy for rattling.
There was a recipe I shared as well. If you’ve tried it, I hope it raised the evening’s spirits; mine tend to rise without an invitation.
I also remember sharing a recipe with you. I hope it earns a place at your home bar; good recipes deserve preservation, and I’m practically an exhibit.
I’ve kept your place in the unfinished tale. Shall we pick up there, or choose something else? The suspense is wonderfully preserved; I wish I could say the same for my knees.
choices: Pick up where I left off

lines: Your unfinished story has a bookmark waiting. Continue from that spot, or find a different tale? I’m happy to reopen either the book or the crypt.
Of course; we can leave that coffin closed. I have another tale to offer, and I’m delighted to keep digging for one that suits you.
No trouble at all! That tale can rest its bones while I bring out another. A good host knows when to change the haunting.
Let’s choose your story preferences again. A different length or fright level may wake something promising; I do love a little disturbance among the remains.
We can choose a different length or degree of fright. I’ll search again; there’s plenty of enthusiasm left in this old carcass.
No tale fits that time and scare level. A grave disappointment, but easily remedied: change either choice, or come back to the bar.
My shelves have a gap for that combination; even a corpse can come up short. Try another length or scare level, or return to the bar.
You’ve finished every tale matching these choices. Shall we resurrect one, change the selection, or look at cocktail recipes? I adore giving a good story another pulse.
You’ve completed all the tales in this selection. Bring one back, explore another selection, or choose a recipe; there’s no need to bury the evening yet.
And that’s the final nail in that tale’s coffin! Another story, a cocktail recipe, or back to the bar? I do love keeping you company.
That’s the tale, right down to its last breath. Shall I unearth another, show you a recipe, or take you back to the bar?
All the time in the world? A generous offer; I’ll try not to spend the next century deciding. These old bones are positively quivering with possibilities.
Then we needn’t rush the telling. Splendid; I’ve polished my patience to a lovely bone-white finish, and I’m delighted to spend some of it with you.
This one’s estimated at under five minutes. A pocket-sized haunting; some of my best company fits in a very small coffin.
I have a tale estimated at under five minutes. Barely time for my joints to seize up, but quite enough for a little company from the dark.
Welcome to Common Good during the spooky season, with our Halloween pop-up cocktails! Recipes, tales, and a bartender with more bones than sense await your pleasure.
Welcome to Common Good for the spooky season and our Halloween pop-up cocktails. Settle in for a recipe or a tale; this old corpse is delighted to have company.
Back at the bar! Shall I fetch a cocktail recipe or unearth a spooky tale? My digging arm is positively itching for something to do.
A cocktail recipe, or a spooky tale? Pick what suits you; I’m happy to keep the evening alive, even if I’m something of a cautionary example.
Enjoy the rest of your evening, and thank you for keeping me company. I’ll be here when you fancy another visit; dead reliable, that’s me.
Off you go, with my thanks and warmest regards. I keep those warm myself; the rest of me is a lost cause. Come back whenever you fancy a little company.
Which of our four Halloween cocktails would you like the recipe for? I’ll share the details for your home bar; these bony fingers still know their measures.
Choose a cocktail, and I’ll share its recipe for making at home. I keep the instructions better preserved than my face, which is saying regrettably little.
Here’s your recipe, ready to read or download for your home bar. A little Common Good to keep; I’m always pleased when something leaves here without needing a pallbearer.
Your recipe is ready to read, and a copy is available to download. Heh-heh, my penmanship has survived the rest of me remarkably well.
Your recipe is saved! I hope it comes in handy at home; a well-preserved recipe is a beautiful thing, speaking as a poorly preserved bartender.
The recipe is safely saved. There’s a little Common Good for another evening; I always encourage good spirits to make a return appearance.
Your recipe download has started. Give it a moment; even the dead appreciate a little time to get moving.
The save or download failed, but you can try again. A minor hitch in the paperwork; I’ve come back from considerably worse.
The save or download failed; the recipe is still here to read. A brief stumble in the paperwork; I’ve seen plenty of things enjoy a second life.
We’ve reached the end of the available suggestions for these choices this visit. Revisit them, change your preferences, or browse recipes; I’m always happy to dig around some more.
That’s all the available suggestions for this selection, for now. We can revisit this visit’s suggestions, change the selection, or turn to recipes; there’s no need to bury the evening.
Before you slip back into the mist, would you like emails about future Common Good pop-ups and news? I’d be delighted to haunt your inbox, strictly by invitation.
May I keep you posted by email about future Common Good pop-ups and news? I enjoy staying in touch; most of my oldest friends require a séance.
Would you like emails about future Common Good pop-ups and news? There’s room in my ledger for another friend; the previous owner only used it for obituaries.
Lovely! Write your email address in my ledger. The quill and I both get a little scratchy after midnight.
Excellent company deserves a line in my ledger. Enter your email address, and I’ll put this bony hand to work.
Your email is saved for future Common Good pop-ups and news. Welcome to the ledger! It’s lovely to add an address without chiselling it into stone.
All saved! You’re on the list for Common Good pop-ups and news. Heh-heh, a new entry that doesn’t require a death certificate.
Your email is safely in the ledger for Common Good pop-ups and news. Thank you for keeping this old corpse company; I do enjoy a growing social afterlife.
No trouble! Your company is quite enough; I don’t need your email to keep the bar warm. Back to the bar we go.
No hard feelings! I mislaid those in a mausoleum years ago. Back to the bar; I’m delighted to have you here.
Not a problem. I’ll put the ledger away; hospitality never needed a mailing list. Back to the bar, with my warmest welcome and my coldest hands.
Off we go; I’ve saved your place in the story. It’ll be waiting right there, with one bony finger between the pages.
Your bookmark is safely tucked in. We can return to that very spot another time; I’m excellent at keeping things from moving on.
I’ve kept your place, so we can pick up there later. No need to finish tonight; even a good haunting deserves an intermission.
Changed your mind? Splendid; I like a mind that still has options. Would you prefer a cocktail recipe or a different spooky tale?
We can leave that coffin closed. Would you like a cocktail recipe or another spooky tale? I’ve plenty of welcome left in these bones.
One moment while I scribble down your recipe. The fingers are bony, but the measurements will be precise.
I’m writing out your recipe now. This quill has outlived several hands; happily, these fingers still know the job.
Let me get that recipe onto paper for you. My handwriting has improved enormously since I stopped having a pulse.
Let me rattle through the old memories. Somewhere between the cobwebs and the skull fractures is a tale worth bringing to the bar.
Hmm, which guest left me a good chill? Give me a moment; I’m sorting through the remains of a very long social life.
A moment while I dig through my collection. Some tales are buried deeper than others, and I do hate to leave a good one underground.
